title: SAT Sets Aside SEBI's Rs 26 Crore Penalty on Coffee Day Enterprises, Orders Fresh Probe
case_name: Appeal by Coffee Day Enterprises Limited against SEBI's penalty and fund-diversion order
citation: Securities Appellate Tribunal, order dated 5 November 2026 (2:1 majority)
card_summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal on 5 November 2026 set aside SEBI's 2023 penalty order against Coffee Day Enterprises Limited and, by a 2:1 majority, called the regulator's probe into the alleged diversion of Rs 3,535 crore from seven subsidiaries to promoter-linked Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates Limited incomplete. SEBI must complete a fresh probe, including on possible insider trading, within six months.
card_tip: Fund transfers between group companies and a promoter-linked entity can draw SEBI scrutiny years later; keep such inter-company flows and board approvals documented and at arm's length.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: HNI (promoter and family-business group). TARGET QUERY: Coffee Day Enterprises SEBI fund diversion case SAT order. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen (the order was carried the same day or next day by at least six financial-news outlets, suggesting reader interest, but no search-volume data was seen). Cross-verified across LiveLawBiz, Storyboard18, Adgully and Kalkine Media, which agree that the SAT, by 2:1 majority on 5 November 2026, set aside SEBI's 24 January 2023 Whole Time Member order and 27 March 2023 Adjudicating Officer order against Coffee Day Enterprises Limited, nullifying the Rs 26 crore penalty, and directed a fresh, time-bound (six-month) investigation into the transfer of about Rs 3,535 crore from seven CDEL subsidiaries to Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates Limited (MACEL), including examination of possible violations of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Sources differ on the exact figure to which one disclosure-related penalty was reduced (Rs 50 lakh per most reports); that figure is omitted from the card as not independently confirmed. The order makes no finding of guilt against any individual; the outcome depends on SEBI's fresh probe.
